display.title: Episode 234: The Island of Treasures
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi marks 234 weeks on the air, an eight-year-old recites a Mishnah about lost objects, and a shipwrecked man becomes king of a mysterious island, with a lesson about this world and the next.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi celebrates the 234th program, four and a half years on the air, with listeners across the United States, and hopes to keep broadcasting until Moshiach comes, then from Yerushalayim. After the Hakochainik march and a sponsor message, an eight-year-old yeshiva student leads the Shema and recites by heart the Mishnah 'Eilu metzios' from Bava Metzia, about which found objects may be kept and which must be returned. Story time tells 'The Island of Treasures': the only survivor of a shipwreck is crowned king of an island and spends its whole treasury beautifying it, only to learn that he must leave, in his old rags, as soon as the next castaway arrives. Uncle Yossi explains the mashal from Pirkei Avos: this world is a corridor to the World to Come, and Torah and mitzvos are the treasures we send ahead. The show closes with the last Sefer Torah contest entrants, news of the Tzivos Hashem newsletter, Yud-Beis Tammuz this Shabbos, and the campaign to buy a letter in the children's Sefer Torah.
display.lesson: This world is a corridor to the World to Come; use your time here to learn Torah and do mitzvos, the treasures you send ahead.
